analysis_steps.goal: Iteratively reconstruct the dust surface density profile Sigma(R) and fit the radial maximum grain size profile a_max^mid(R)

method.value: Divide the disk midplane (out to 80 AU) into 32 radial bins of width 2.5 AU. Initialize a_max^mid(R) with a power law (a_max0 = 1000 um, b = 6 at R0 = 40 AU) and fix a_max^mid = 10 cm for R < 20 AU. Sequentially from inner to outer bins, perform a dense logarithmic grid search of a_max^mid to fit the observed spectral index alpha_mm(R). For every trial model, iteratively adjust Sigma(R) from scratch using the 2.9 mm observed-to-model radial intensity ratio until convergence (<5% change, ~12 iterations). Estimate uncertainties using 17 logarithmically spaced models in [log(a_best)-0.4, log(a_best)+0.4] per bin weighted by 1/chi^2.

claims.hypothesis: Dust grain size in the DS Tau protoplanetary disk varies with radius following an inside-out decreasing trend predicted by dust evolution and radial drift theories.
claims.experiment: Simultaneously fit the SED and spatially resolved ALMA Band 6 (1.3 mm) and Band 3 (2.9 mm) radial brightness and spectral index profiles using self-consistent RADMC-3D radiative transfer models across 32 radial bins.
claims.result: The best-fit maximum grain size in the midplane decreases from 10 cm in the inner disk (R < 20 AU) to ~30 um in the outer disk.
claims.finding: The DS Tau disk exhibits an outside-in increasing (inside-out decreasing) grain size profile consistent with theoretical expectations of radial drift and dust evolution.

evidence.quote: The best-fit grain sizes range from centimeters in the inner disk down to ${\sim}\,30\,\mu{\rm m}$ in the outer regions. Such an inside-out decreasing tendency is consistent with theories of dust evolution.
We find that the grain size increases from ${\sim}\,30\,\mu \rm m$ in the outer disk to centimeters in the inner regions.

claims.hypothesis: A discontinuity in the radial grain size profile exists at the interface between the gap and the ring in the DS Tau disk.
claims.experiment: Compare best-fit radiative transfer models (using both DSHARP and silicate-carbon dust opacities) against alternative models where the grain size profile is smoothed across the gap-ring boundary or peaks in the ring center.
claims.result: Grain size increases by two orders of magnitude (DSHARP) or shows a one-order-of-magnitude bump (silicate-carbon) at the gap-ring boundary (R ~ 50 AU); smoothing this feature or placing larger grains in the ring center fails to reproduce the observed spectral index profile.
claims.finding: A discontinuity in grain size at the gap-ring boundary is required by current data, though its amplitude depends on the assumed dust opacity model and higher-resolution observations are needed to resolve small-scale variations.

evidence.quote: Moreover, our modeling also indicates that at the interface region between the gap and the ring, the grain size profile shows a discontinuity, with its amplitude dependent on the dust model adopted in the radiative transfer analysis.

One model features a relatively smooth profile of $a_{\rm max}^{\rm mid}$, i.e., there is no jump in $a_{\rm max}^{\rm mid}$ in the border between the gap and ring. The resulting spectral indices are shown with the yellow solid line in the top panel of Figure 2. In the other model, $a_{\rm max}^{\rm mid}(s)$ in the ring are devised to be larger than those in the gap. The result is indicated with the green solid line. It is clear that both setups cannot reproduce the observation.

claims.hypothesis: The dust mass depleted from the gap in DS Tau is sufficient to form the ~3.5 M_Jup planet proposed by hydrodynamic simulations.
claims.experiment: Construct a smooth power-law dust surface density profile across the gap (between 6 AU and 60 AU) and integrate the difference relative to the best-fit surface density profile.
claims.result: Approximately 2 M_Jup of dust has been depleted within the gap.
claims.finding: Accounting for a typical gas-to-dust mass ratio (~30), the depleted mass within the gap is sufficient to form a 3.5 M_Jup planet.

evidence.quote: Based on the best-fit model, we find that dust of ${\sim}\,2$ Jupiter masses has been depleted within the gap. By taking the gas-to-dust mass ratio into account, the lost mass is enough to form the 3.5 Jupiter mass planet inferred by literature hydrodynamic simulations.

why_this_method.value: Self-consistent 3D radiative transfer modeling with isotropic scattering accounts for the coupling between dust temperature, vertical structure, surface density, and grain size, while image-plane fitting allows iterative scaling of the dust surface density directly from the optically thinner 2.9 mm brightness profile.

evidence.quote: Given the stellar parameters, dust density distribution and dust opacities, the code self-consistently computes the dust temperature using the Monte Carlo approach, and then simulates the SED and millimeter images.

Fitting the ALMA observations is performed in the image plane, rather than in the interferometric (u, v) space, because the construction of the dust surface density is directly linked to the brightness profile, see Sect. 4.2.1.

evidence.loc: Iteration for the dust surface density
evidence.quote: Choosing 2.9 mm instead of 1.3 mm is due to the fact that the disk is optically thinner at longer wavelengths. Hence, the 2.9 mm ALMA image better traces the dust density distribution.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Constant maximum grain size with radius and parametric Gaussian-depleted power-law surface density (rejected because it cannot simultaneously fit Band 6 and Band 3 surface brightness profiles and the radially varying spectral index)

evidence.quote: However, within the whole parameter space composed of $\gamma$, $M_{\mathrm {dust}}$ and $a^{\mathrm {mid}}_{\mathrm {max}}$, it is challenging to simultaneously fit the surface brightnesses at both ALMA bands.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single power-law radial profile for midplane maximum grain size a_max^mid(R) = a_max0 (R/R_0)^-b (rejected because the best model cannot simultaneously fit the two ALMA images)

evidence.loc: Grid search for the maximum grain sizes in the midplane
evidence.quote: The best model ($a_{\max0}\,{=}\,1000\,\mu{\rm m}$, $b\,{=}\,6$) cannot simultaneously fit the two ALMA images, implying that the maximum grain size in the midplane of DS Tau’s disk cannot be represented by a simple power-law function.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Snow line condensation front as the cause of the grain size jump at the gap-ring boundary (rejected because the midplane temperature there is ~10 K, not associated with main volatile snow lines)

evidence.quote: However, according to our model, the midplane temperature at the boundary between the gap and ring is about 10 K which is not associated with condensation fronts of main volatile species in protoplanetary disks.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Smooth grain size profile across the gap-ring boundary or larger grains in the ring than in the gap (rejected because both setups fail to reproduce the observed spectral index profile)

evidence.quote: One model features a relatively smooth profile of $a_{\rm max}^{\rm mid}$, i.e., there is no jump in $a_{\rm max}^{\rm mid}$ in the border between the gap and ring. The resulting spectral indices are shown with the yellow solid line in the top panel of Figure 2. In the other model, $a_{\rm max}^{\rm mid}(s)$ in the ring are devised to be larger than those in the gap. The result is indicated with the green solid line. It is clear that both setups cannot reproduce the observation.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Surface density iteration stopped after ~12 iterations when adjacent iterations changed by <5% at all radii; 32 radial bins of 2.5 AU (1/8 of the ALMA beam) were chosen because finer bins require more computation without significantly affecting results.

evidence.loc: Iteration for the dust surface density
evidence.quote: According to our experiments, convergence can be achieved after about 12 iterations when the surface density of two adjacent iterations changes by less than $5\%$ at any radius.

evidence.loc: Grid search for the maximum grain sizes in the midplane
evidence.quote: The width of each part is only one-eighth of the size of the ALMA beam, meaning that our setup is sufficient for resolving the disk substructures. Using more radial bins will take more computational resources, and the effect on the results is not significant.

limitations_admitted.value: The inner disk (R < 20 AU) is optically thick even at 2.9 mm, so the grain size there cannot be constrained by the spectral index and is fixed to 10 cm.

evidence.loc: Grid search for the maximum grain sizes in the midplane
evidence.quote: After many simulation tests, we found that this inner region is optically thick even at 2.9 mm, indicating that the grain size can no longer be constrained by the observed spectral index.

limitations_admitted.value: Fluctuations in the retrieved grain size profile occur on spatial scales smaller than the beam size (~20 AU), requiring future higher-resolution observations to confirm.

evidence.quote: The $a^{\mathrm {mid}}_{\mathrm {max}}\,{-}\,R$ profile exhibits some fluctuations on spatial scales smaller than the beam size. Future high-resolution observations are desired to confirm their reality.
However, the measured spectral indices actually trace the mean dust properties over a radius range depending on the beam size, i.e., ${\sim}\,20\,\rm{AU}$ in our case.

limitations_admitted.value: The amplitude and shape of the grain size discontinuity at the gap-ring boundary depend on the assumed dust opacity model.

evidence.quote: Moreover, our modeling also indicates that at the interface region between the gap and the ring, the grain size profile shows a discontinuity, with its amplitude dependent on the dust model adopted in the radiative transfer analysis.

referee_caveats_inferred: Fitting 32 radial bins of 2.5 AU width to images with a ~16-20 AU beam without spatial regularization introduces strong bin-to-bin degeneracies and beam-smearing artifacts, especially at sharp intensity gradients like the gap-ring edge.
The sequential inside-out bin-by-bin search does not guarantee a global minimum across all 32 coupled radial bins because beam convolution mixes emission from adjacent bins.
Isotropic scattering is used in RADMC-3D, whereas centimeter- and millimeter-sized grains have strongly forward-peaked phase functions that can alter effective albedo and spectral index.
